text: {"edits": [{"finding_ids": ["app/stock.py:13:test-failure"], "search": "    return StockLevel(sku=sku, units=reading)", "replace": "    return StockLevel(sku=sku, units=int(reading))", "explanation": "Pydantic V2 only converts floats to int when the fractional part is zero (migration.md#type-conversion-from-floats-to-integers), so passing 3.7 raises int_from_float. No import changes are needed."}], "notes": "The only finding is the fractional-float-to-int ValidationError in from_scale. The fix is an explicit int() truncation at the call site, which keeps the documented truncate intent and avoids relying on V1's implicit float coercion. StockLevel itself is unchanged, since units: int is correct for whole-unit counts. No deprecated V1 APIs appear in this file (no .dict(), .parse_obj(), class Config, or validators), so no other edits are needed. total_units and the imports are left as they are. Note that int() truncates toward zero, which matches the comment's \"truncate\" wording for positive readings."}
